title: Pre-registered tests on Utah-array motor cortex data: decoding-ceiling test inconclusive; SBP lag-1 participation ratio saturated far before decoding. Post hoc: no ceiling up to 96-192 electrodes
abstract: Question: does decoding quality from motor-cortex Utah arrays stop at a ceiling as electrode count N grows, and does neural dimensionality saturate at the same N? Data: BrainGate dSNR electrode-subsampling curves (Hahn et al. 2026; 15 curves, 7 participants, N = 6-96 per array, up to 192 for two arrays), monkey LINK finger data (DANDI 001201, 8 sessions) and human FALCON H1 data (DANDI 000954, 6 days). Pre-registered results: (1) The saturation test on 10 held-out curves from 4 participants (fit N <= 40, predict N >= 48) was inconclusive: a saturating information-limited model beat log2 growth in 7 of 10 curves but in only 2 of 4 participants, and log2 over-predicted at the largest N in 0 of 10 curves (it under-predicted in all 15). (2) The test that lag-1 participation-ratio (PR) dimensionality saturates where decoding saturates failed: for spike-band power (SBP) in held-out LINK sessions, PR reached 80% of its full value at about 7 electrodes and decoding at about 52 (ratio 0.13, 95% CI 0.11-0.26; band 0.5-2). For threshold crossings the ratio was near 1, but neither curve saturated, so that result is not diagnostic. Post-hoc results: no BrainGate curve reached a ceiling in the tested range; the dSNR gain per doubling stayed above 0 and the local log-log slope stayed >= 0.28. Growth was faster than log2, which independent sqrt(N) pooling also predicts, and slower than sqrt(N) at large N: the local slope fell from about 0.75 at 6->12 to below 0.5 at 48->96 in 14 of 15 curves (7 of 7 participants). This is a diminishing return beyond independent pooling, not a ceiling. A saturating hyperbola fits the full range best, but its fitted constants contradict the observed rising gains; if a ceiling is hyperbolic, the data put 90% of it above about 430 electrodes in 14 of 15 curves. In the spiking data, with independent electrode subsets per session and three decoders, the gain per doubling stayed above 0 up to 96 electrodes in 60 of 60 runs and was roughly constant above about 24 electrodes; whether it rose from small N depended on the decoder. The early-saturating SBP component is broad, non-directional and movement-locked. Limitations: session-averaged curves from one closed-loop OLS estimator, simple decoders with modest R2 in the spiking data, a self-attested pre-registration time, and a lag-1 PR that is not trial-averaged task dimensionality.

display.caption: Pre-registered test (inconclusive): log2 and information-limited models fitted on N <= 40 (grey band) and extrapolated to N >= 48. Log2 under-predicted at the largest N in every curve.

Pre-registered Part B: decoding SNR and lag-1 / lag-0 participation-ratio dimensionality versus electrode count, normalized to the full pool. SBP lag-1 PR saturated at about 7 electrodes while decoding kept rising; for threshold crossings no curve saturated.

Post hoc: BrainGate dSNR gain per doubling (normalized to the 6->12 gain) and local log-log slope, with log2 and independent-pooling sqrt(N) references. Gains rose more slowly than the sqrt(N) null; the slope fell below 0.5 at 48->96 in 14 of 15 curves but stayed above 0 (T6 and T5 Combined show a small fall in gain at the top).
